units.note: Unit of randomization for genotype in field trials.
Unit for hard-to-randomize factors (irrigation) in split-plot designs.
Usual experimental unit in greenhouse; may hold several plants.
Experimental unit only if each plant is individually randomized.
Almost always a subsample.
Unit when watering or treatment is per tray.
Unit for temperature/CO2/light treatments; one chamber per treatment = no replication.
Unit when treatment is given individually (injection, gavage).
Unit when treatment is in diet/drinking water.
Unit for maternal/prenatal treatments.
Biological replicate for cells, organoids, single-cell data.
Independent experiments are the replicates.
One per biological sample.
Extraction batch should be randomized and recorded.
Unit for genotype in tray experiments if each cell is randomized.
Repeat of a chamber experiment; acts as a block.
Unit for food/drug treatments; flies are subsamples.
Source of flies; block by bottle.
Unit when feed, water or housing treatments are applied to a group of animals.
Unit when a grazing system, ration or management practice is applied to a whole herd or paddock.
Fish sharing a tank share water, temperature and feeding; the tank is the unit for these treatments.
Embryos or seeds treated together in one dish share the treatment; the dish is the unit.
Independent culture flask; the unit for treatments of microbial or algal cultures.
Each bioreactor or chemostat is one unit; samples over time from one vessel are repeated measures.
Like a pot: plants sharing a bucket share soil and watering.
